correctness.rationale: The sign-pattern proof exhausts all generic six-vertex configurations of the centered triangular prism. Spherical excess on the exact hexagonal normal cone gives p3; Haar lune angles on all nine prism edges give the expected vertex number, which forces p4 and p5. Direct differentiation yields a strictly decreasing stationarity function with opposite endpoint signs, establishing one global optimum. A deterministic independent edge-crossing checker passed 1,100,000 sampled normals and numerical derivative/root checks; simulations do not substitute for the proof.
